input.description: Map sellm agent code architecture
input.prompt:
Repo: /home/amiad/Desktop/taco-sellm (branch main). This is a buyer negotiation agent for the Tacto Negotiation Arena (context in docs/CONTEXT.md, sections 4-8 and 14). I need a precise architecture map of OUR agent code in sellm/ on main, so we can rewrite it from scratch. Thoroughness: very thorough. Read the code, don't skim.

Report, with file:line references:
1. Entry point: how `--agent sellm` is wired (arena_kit/cli.py AGENTS, sellm/agent.py make_agent, KNOBS / CALC_KNOBS). What object is returned and what `decide(case, threads)` does step by step.
2. sellm/negotiator.py (879 lines): the full decision procedure per move: first ask, step sizing, when it accepts, when it walks, how it handles final_offer/agreed/RFQ multiple suppliers, timeouts, round limit, term sheets (how many, which fields), how e-mail text is produced (template? writer.py? LLM?). List every knob with its default and what it changes.
3. sellm/calculator.py: how it prices packages (uses arena_kit.cost.total_cost? relationship term with which supplier estimate?), how it picks payment_days, contract_months, volume, effective_date, index_clause, incoterm etc. What "expected end price" means and how it's estimated.
4. sellm/claims.py: the argument bank: which fact kinds (idx, quote, sc, qn, po, cost, fc, news, doc+ctr), how they are chosen, verified offline against facts.json, one per e-mail, dedupe.
5. sellm/endgame.py, sellm/advisor.py, sellm/writer.py, sellm/llm.py, sellm/personas.py: what each does and whether it's actually used in the default --agent sellm path.
6. sellm/intel/ (dossier): what a dossier contains (fields, signals vocabulary like cash_pressure, material_hedged, list_price_fixed, capacity_tight, informal_costing), how it is built from data/package and the case overlay, how the negotiator consumes it. Where the 46 dossiers live (sellm/dossiers/).
7. sellm/runner.py: final runner modes (per-thread vs per-case turns), wave handling, closing before the cap, resume, deadline per move, logging. Does it call arena_kit.cli.pull_first? Does it ever touch forbidden endpoints (/v1/events, /screen, /leaderboard, /results)?
8. tests/: which test files exist for sellm (test_runner, test_claims, test_intel, test_sellm_agent, test_endgame...), what they assert, how long they run.
9. arena_kit pieces our code relies on: arena_kit/cost.py (total_cost, cost_breakdown, supplier_value, relationship_cost, complete_offer, snap, must_haves_ok), arena_kit/play.py (play, play_waves, closing_move, latest, standing), arena_kit/docs.py (quote_terms, standard_terms), arena_kit/data.py (DataPackage). Summarize their signatures and gotchas.
10. Anything that looks like dead code, duplicated logic, fragile hacks, case-specific hardcoding (case IDs or supplier IDs in code), or known bugs (TODO/FIXME).

Be concrete and complete; this will be used to design a from-scratch rewrite. Keep the report structured, max ~2500 words.

input.description: Map branches and score history
input.prompt:
Repo: /home/amiad/Desktop/taco-sellm. A team of 3 builds a buyer negotiation agent (Tacto Negotiation Arena; context docs/CONTEXT.md). Remote branches: origin/main, origin/jonathans_branch, origin/omars_branch. Use only read-only git commands (git log, git show, git diff, git branch -a; do NOT checkout, fetch, pull or modify anything). Thoroughness: very thorough.

I need the LEARNING CURVE: which code change produced which measured score change.
1. `git log --format='%h %ad %an %s' --date=format:'%a %H:%M' -- sellm/ arena_kit/` on main: build a chronological table: commit, author, what changed in the agent, and the score measured with it (find the matching [run]/[change] entries in docs/LOG.md and runs/README.md, scoreboard in docs/STATUS.md). Key milestones I know of: kit LLM baseline 61.5; negotiator v1.2 67.5; v1.4 72.4; sellm@7a49c38 72.9; jonathans_branch@67001e7 74.9 (clause offer, P02 0.531->0.725); omars_branch E2g (P18 0.467->0.520), runner one loop per case (P05 0.820). Fill in everything between, including reverted / rejected experiments and their numbers.
2. jonathans_branch vs main: `git log main..origin/jonathans_branch`, `git diff main...origin/jonathans_branch --stat` and the substance of the code diff (sellm/endgame.py clause_offer etc.). Summarize exactly what logic it adds.
3. omars_branch vs main: same. Includes Negotiator.hedged(), idx_recent knob (E2/E2g), runner default one loop per case (--turns), experiments/LEDGER.md, SESSION_HANDOFF.md. Summarize the logic and the measured results; read experiments/LEDGER.md and SESSION_HANDOFF.md on that branch via `git show origin/omars_branch:path`.
4. Per hosted practice case (P01 P02 P03 P04 P05 P07 P08 P10 P11 P18): the best score ever reached, by which agent/commit, and the current main score; the C_open, C_best (from runs/README.md).
5. A list of every experiment that was tried and REJECTED or made things worse, with the number and the reason (e.g. LLM writer 71.6 not repeatable, LLM advisor accept made P01/P18 worse, no qn after sc, contract at horizon P08 0.538, idx argument to hedged supplier P08 0.438, one loop per thread in RFQ 0.665).

Output a structured report (max ~2500 words) with tables. Exact numbers and commit hashes matter.

input.description: Analyze per-case negotiation runs
input.prompt:
Repo: /home/amiad/Desktop/taco-sellm. Buyer negotiation agent for the Tacto Negotiation Arena (rules: docs/CONTEXT.md sections 3-7). Every practice/sandbox session the team played is saved under runs/practice/<case>/ and runs/sandbox/ (.md readable transcripts with supplier reasons/trace, .json raw), indexed in runs/README.md; analysis in runs/BASELINE.md. Thoroughness: very thorough. Read-only.

Goal: for each hosted practice case P01 P02 P03 P04 P05 P07 P08 P10 P11 P18, figure out WHERE THE REMAINING POINTS ARE and what supplier behaviour determines them, so a rewritten agent can capture them. For each case:
1. C_open, C_best, best score reached and its deal terms (from the best session's .md), current typical score with --agent sellm (sessions labelled sellm, ~72.9 run at 00:45 and jonathans_branch@67001e7 run at 02:20).
2. The supplier's concession path in the best sessions: opening terms, each counter, when it said final_offer, what it refused, the trace "reasons" text (the supplier's internal reasoning: e.g. needs boss approval, cost floor, reacts to tone, wants faster payment, index clause). Quote the key reason lines.
3. What the C_best term sheet probably looks like (which levers: price, payment_days, effective_date, contract_months, volume, index_clause, lead_time, ppm/chargeback) vs what we got, and the cost breakdown gap (cost_breakdown parts) between our deal and C_best if visible.
4. Which arguments/facts got 'verified' and which moved the supplier vs 'that's not our reality'.
Also read runs/BASELINE.md, experiments/RESULTS.md (sandbox probe findings, section 5 rules), experiments/PRICE-PATH.md, experiments/PERSISTENCE.md, experiments/PRACTICE-ARMS.md and summarize their concrete rules about supplier behaviour (mirroring concessions, final offer is final, first ask level, lowball penalty, step sizes, how many rounds are worth it).

Output: a per-case table plus per-case bullet notes, then a list of general supplier-behaviour rules with evidence (session ids). Max ~3000 words. Exact numbers matter.

content.text: Während die drei Explore-Agents laufen, lese ich die zentralen Dokumente selbst.

result.output:
1	# LEARNINGS - what works and what fails in negotiations
2	
3	Durable findings with their evidence. Add one when a replay, a cost breakdown or an offline
4	calculation teaches something that should change how the agent behaves. State how sure we are:
5	**confirmed** (seen in our own replay), **computed** (from the cost function), **reported** (from
6	Tacto's docs or FAQ, not yet seen by us). Raw history goes to `docs/LOG.md`.
7	
8	## General
9	
10	- **Tone and relationship move price** (reported, FAQ P01 recording). Appreciation for past
11	  fairness plus one verified index plus an offer to pay faster got 0.76. The same index sent as an
12	  ultimatum got EUR 136.50 from November instead of January, about EUR 13,700 a year worse.
13	- **Price is only one lever, and often not the biggest** (computed, P01 below). The kit's naive
14	  agent negotiates price only and leaves the other fields at the supplier's opening values.
15	- **The kit agents ignore the relationship term** (confirmed in code). In `stabilise` and
16	  `secure_supply` cases the arena charges for leaving the supplier below its sustainable margin;
17	  `total_cost` only includes it when given a supplier estimate. Our P01 deal at EUR 135.40 showed
18	  `relationship: 0.0` in the arena's breakdown, so that price did not squeeze Brandlhuber.
19	- **Answer "which figures?" with data** (reported, FAQ P01 recording). The supplier asked for the
20	  basis of our price; citing the should-cost estimate (`cost:310010`) was `verified` and brought
21	  the closing offer.
22	- **Trust the numbers, not the supplier's prose** (reported, `brief/api.md`,
23	  `data/package/KNOWN_ISSUES.md`). Term sheets and the generated documents (quote PDF, cost
24	  breakdown, 8D report, delivery schedule, order confirmation) are "rendered from the supplier's
25	  structured state, never written by a language model, byte-stable" - their figures are exact and
26	  bind. The e-mail body's reasoning is in-character colour, not fact-checked: "cheaper engineering
27	  variants a supplier mentions are information, not binding terms," and identical messages need
28	  not get identical replies. P01's letter blames energy costs while the cited index shows
29	  electricity (PPI-D351) fell 3.7 % over the period (see below) - read a stated reason as a signal
30	  of what the supplier cares about, not as a checked fact.
31	  Our own `facts.json` is the one checked ground truth for what *we* cite, and it has documented,
32	  deliberate quirks, not errors: `should_cost` carries a stated error (5 % where a plant-specific
33	  estimate exists, 5-15 % otherwise, with `confidence_pct` in `facts.json`); `sup:71999` and
34	  `sup:70210` are the same company under an old/new record; some PO lines carry a stale price
35	  (`price_note: stale_condition`); OTD differs 10-30 points depending on which of three delivery
36	  dates (requested, confirmed, goods-receipt) you read; ppm is jumpy on small lots, so read the
37	  rolling scorecard. Pick the right reference before citing, and build the argument bank only from
38	  IDs checked against `facts.json`, never from a supplier's stated reasons.
39	
40	## From the P02 argument tests (Sun 01:20-02:10, 8 practice sessions; `experiments/P02-ARGUMENTS.md` on `jonathans_branch`)
41	
42	Nordmark (P02) ended at EUR 371.66 with 90 days in more than ten sessions, whatever was asked or
43	argued. One session per untested kind of argument, on top of `--agent sellm`:
44	
45	- **An index clause is security for a supplier, and it pays for it with price - far more than the
46	  clause costs us** (confirmed, P02). Asked for the copper clause with the 5 % deadband (cost to us:
47	  0.8 % of spend), Nordmark's first answer was 351.45 instead of 373.97: "we agree to introduce the
48	  CU-NOTATION index clause to reduce the base price". Its letter passes copper on; the clause does
49	  that for it.
50	- **With a relationship term the lowest price is not the best one, and code has to choose the
51	  price** (confirmed, computed). The arena counts a clause as security, not cash: 351.45 is 5.8 %
52	  below Nordmark's full cost and cost us EUR 119,974 in the relationship term - score 0.242, worse
53	  than the fixed price (0.531). Our total cost is lowest at 361.35 (score 0.735): there the next
54	  euro off the price costs more in the relationship term than it saves.
55	- **A supplier never raises a price it has named** (confirmed, P02): asked 361.35 after its own
56	  351.45 ("we do not want a price that leaves you below a sustainable margin") it answered twice
57	  "our offer of EUR 351.45 is economically viable and remains our official position". Asked 361.35
58	  at once, it agreed in its first reply. So an ask the supplier may undercut must already be the
59	  price we want: never open below it on a structure that gives the supplier security.
60	- **Two sheets in the first e-mail work as a menu** (confirmed, P02): the fixed-price ask and the
61	  clause at our price - it agreed to the clause sheet at once (362.70, score 0.725; the price came
62	  from our own cost estimate, capped by its opening).
63	- **A fixed-price wall can be the supplier's cost floor exactly** (computed from two relationship
64	  charges, to the euro): Nordmark's full cost is EUR 367.56 at a cost of money of 6.67 %, and 371.66
65	  with 90 days is worth exactly that to it. No argument goes below it: "below this price we would
66	  need facts, not just a lower number".
67	- **A fact the arena calls `irrelevant` is not free** (confirmed 2 of 2, P02): an index that is not a
68	  cost driver of the part (producer prices of electric motors, electricity) and order prices or the
69	  forecast of another part of the same supplier came back `irrelevant`; the verified fact next to
70	  them lost its effect (the forecast moved it 0.46 instead of 1.91) and it said `final_offer` after
71	  three messages instead of four (0.394 and 0.319 against 0.531). Cite only facts about this part
72	  and its cost drivers.
73	- **Not levers on Nordmark** (one session each): answering its question "which volume can you
74	  commit to?" with the contract's binding volume and a call-off schedule (0.525), asking it to put
75	  our proposal before its pricing committee (0.480). Earlier, by Amiad: past renewals asked vs
76	  settled, more arguments per e-mail, a warmer or a coercive tone.
77	
78	## From the practice arms (Sat 21:15-21:35, 30 practice sessions; `experiments/PRACTICE-ARMS.md`)
79	
80	One change per arm on the real practice suppliers, base `19b339f`. Per-case scores and the code of
81	the arms are in `experiments/PRACTICE-ARMS.md` and `experiments/arms/`.
82	
83	- **Practice suppliers answer identical messages with identical numbers** (confirmed: v1.1 twice,
84	  9 of 10 cases identical; D01 x3). One session per single-supplier case is a fair comparison; only
85	  RFQ threads move with timing (P05 0.659-0.769). Replaying a variant over recorded sessions says
86	  which cases it changes before any session is spent (`experiments/arms/tools/replay.py`).
87	- **A verified fact moves a supplier by 1-2 %, on some suppliers** (confirmed): P01 0.831 -> 0.915
88	  (notice letter `doc`+`ctr`, should-cost, forecast; "we did not know that - a fair point"), P02
89	  0.293 -> 0.531 (price history `po`, forecast, OTD). It did not move P04, P07, P08, P18 ("it holds,
90	  but it does not change our calculation").
91	- **The arena reads integers with a thousands comma as something else** (confirmed 4 of 4):
92	  "2,376 ppm", "5,263 ppm", "27,778 ppm" came back `contradicted` and cost trust ("That costs
93	  trust"); "2376 ppm" was `verified`. EUR amounts with decimals and forecast units were fine.
94	  Write ppm and other integer figures without a thousands separator.
95	- **Topics count once per case, not IDs** (confirmed, P07, P11): after one forecast `fc:` of one part
96	  another part's forecast is `duplicate`; a complaint `qn:` after the scorecard's quality `sc:` is
97	  `duplicate`. Verified together in one case: index, notice letter + contract, should-cost, price
98	  history, forecast, on-time delivery, quality record.
99	- **A `duplicate` citation still works; a round without an argument gets a hold** (confirmed,
100	  Sat 22:16): dropping the `qn:` that followed an `sc:` cost P11 0.778 -> 0.710 (the supplier held
101	  45.50 from the first argument-free round on, "we are really at the limit", instead of accepting
102	  45.09) and P02 0.531 -> 0.522. The supplier reads the sentence ("that quality complaint ... was
103	  already baked into our last price drop") and keeps conceding. Keep sending an argument each round.
104	- **The supplier's final price on a given structure does not depend on our first ask** (confirmed
105	  on P04 4.09 vs 4.54, P11 38.88 vs 42.41, P18 5.02 vs 4.89): suppliers follow their own concession
106	  schedule. What our ask changes is which alternative sheets they put next to their offer.
107	- **Asking for an index clause's deadband is priced by the supplier** (confirmed, mixed): P08 it
108	  moved from 5.35 to 5.55-5.59 (0.549 -> 0.42-0.46), P18 it gave the 5 % variant for +0.10
109	  (0.386 -> 0.467-0.485). Take a deadband variant the supplier quotes when C prefers it; do not
110	  assume the price stays.
111	- **The dossier is worth about 3.5 points on the six cases tested** (confirmed, 6 cases: 5 better,
112	  1 equal, `no dossier` vs `full`). For a supplier without one the agent sends two equal-C offers
113	  (quoted days and 90 days) and loses little.
114	- **Bundles: contract length beyond the horizon is not free** (open, P07): 5.41 for 36 months here,
115	  5.36 for 24 months from the kit agent; not yet tested one against the other.
116	
117	## From the negotiator's sandbox runs (Sat 18:40-20:20, 29 free sessions; `experiments/RESULTS.md` section 7)
118	
119	- **Suppliers price in value** (`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value`): a later start date or longer
120	  payment is paid for in the price (D01: first counter 51.30 / 51.50 / 51.80 for December /
121	  February / April, the same worth to the foundry). Contract length was free. So: ask for coverage,
122	  trade cash terms only where the supplier's cost of money differs from ours.
123	- **With two or three term sheets the supplier answers the one worth most to it** (65 of 79
124	  replies), not the one cheapest for us. It answers on our structure in 294 of 304 replies.
125	- **The step must fit the gap.** The foundry gives back half of our step, the job shop all of it
126	  and asks for "bigger steps". Sizing each step from the gap, the rounds left and the share it has
127	  given back so far beat fixed steps on both cases (D01 0.894 -> 0.920, D02 0.448 -> 0.530).
128	- **Citing the rival's standing offer moved the second bidder at once** (16.40 -> 15.40, "we are
129	  prepared to match the competing offer"), with the claim `verified`.
130	- **Take the trade a supplier names**: "If you can pay in 14 days, I can come down" came as an
131	  alternative sheet; sending that sheet back closed 0.2 lower.
132	- **A bidder that says `agreed` is not automatically the best offer**; close on the cheapest
133	  standing offer. A leader left waiting timed out and its offer got worse (14.50 -> 14.60).
134	- **In all five real cases with a relationship term the opening itself carried none** (D01, P01,
135	  P02, P03, P10), and the suppliers' final offers sat near their sustainable margin (D01: 3.3-4.0 %
136	  against 4 %). Backed out of the results: full cost / opening price was 0.909 (D01), 0.938 (P01),
137	  0.899 (P03); the should-cost of the supplier's own plant was 2 % above the true full cost in
138	  both cases where we can check it (P01, P03).
139	
140	## From the sandbox probes (Sat 15:42-15:57, 33 free sessions)
141	
142	Evidence and tables: `experiments/RESULTS.md`. Measured on the sandbox's demo suppliers only.
143	
144	- **Only the first term sheet of an e-mail can be accepted** (confirmed, 4 of 4: `422 not a
145	  standing offer`). To take a supplier's second package, send its exact terms back as our sheet;
146	  the supplier answers `agreed` and that sheet can be accepted (confirmed, 2 of 2).
147	- **A final offer is final** (confirmed, 8 sessions). Pushing the price after `final_offer` gained
148	  nothing and lost the deal once in two tries. A holding message without a term sheet keeps the
149	  offer alive and restarts the clock.
150	- **P02 also withdrew after a post-final-offer price push** (confirmed, 2026-10-11, replay
151	  `1a882885bd67dea7`): with the LLM writing the e-mails, a buyer ladder of EUR 1.00, 46.89, 92.78
152	  led Nordmark to EUR 373.85 at 90-day payment and `final_offer`; our next ask, EUR 138.68, ended the
153	  session with no deal (score 0.000). The requested ten rounds were impossible once the supplier
154	  withdrew. Do not push after `final_offer`; the one-euro anchor also did not bring the supplier near
155	  the buyer's EUR 368.14 target. Three follow-up branches at EUR 370.00, 369.03, and 368.14 after
156	  `final_offer` (EUR 373.95, 373.90, 373.85 respectively) all ended in withdrawal and score 0.000.
157	  A fourth run offered EUR 370.00 after `final_offer` at EUR 373.80 and answered Nordmark's stated
158	  arguments point by point: weighted input exposure, historic purchase prices, financing premium,
159	  and the missing price bridge. The seller still withdrew (replay `80108787b179d871`); stronger
160	  argumentation did not change the post-final-offer outcome.
161	- **The supplier mirrors our steps, not our level** (confirmed on D01, 20 sessions). Its first
162	  counter did not depend on our opening. It then gave back 0.6-0.85 of each step we made and said
163	  `final_offer` at our 6th message. Opening 1.00 lower with the same steps changed nothing; steps
164	  of 0.40 instead of 0.15 moved the score from about 0.77 to 0.89. Steps of 0.05 got 0.68 and an
165	  early final offer. **Open low, concede in about five large steps, never shrink the steps early.**
166	  Not yet confirmed on a practice supplier.
167	- **RFQ: one loop per thread** (confirmed). It removes the timeouts. A supplier at `final_offer`
168	  left waiting for over a minute withdrew. After a timeout the offer ID changes.
169	- **A rival's offer cited by its ID is `verified`** (confirmed); the same ID twice is `duplicate`.
170	- **An early `agreed` means the ask was too high** (seen in D02): both RFQ suppliers have far more
171	  room than any run found (C_best 156,739, best closed about 186,000).
172	
173	## From the lab (Sat 16:00-17:00, `sellm/lab/`, `runs/lab/`)
174	
175	How the twins were built and how well they match: `runs/lab/BACKTEST.md`, `runs/lab/VALIDATION.md`.
176	
177	- **A supplier's floor is its full cost in cash terms, and C_best pins it down** (computed, two
178	  routes). The floor that makes the cheapest acceptable package cost exactly C_best is 129.91 for
179	  P01; the relationship charge the arena billed on our P01 deal implies 129.95. Where a
180	  plant-specific should-cost exists, floors are within 3-5 % of it. So **should-cost is a good
181	  estimate of the floor**, and the floor is in value terms: faster payment, a longer lead time or an
182	  index clause lower the price the supplier can accept.
183	- **Suppliers price levers at their own cost** (seen in their alternative sheets): payment days at
184	  about 6.5 % a year for groups (P02, P08), about 9 % for a family foundry (D01), about 35 % for a
185	  Czech job shop (P05: 16 days faster = 0.50 on 32); lead time about 0.15 EUR per unit per day
186	  shorter (P10); 1,200 ppm tighter about 1.40 EUR per unit (P11). A trade is good for us when its
187	  value to us is above that.
188	  Measured over every saved session (Sat 22:15, replies with two sheets that differ only in payment
189	  days, yearly rate = price step / mean price / day step x 360), against the dossier's
190	  `cost_of_money`: P02 70510 0.066 and P08 70710 0.065 (group, dossier 0.065); P03 70530 0.041
191	  (group, 0.065); P04 70620 0.073 and P07 70610 0.075 (family, 0.09); P18 70740 0.11-0.22 (family,
192	  0.09; it also wrote "we have already reached our limit for these extended payment terms");

8	## 1. Where the points are
9	
10	The final ranks the mean score per case, on hidden cases with suppliers we have not met. So the
11	agent must be good on average and must never throw a case away. Points come from three places:
12	
13	1. **Structure of the deal - arithmetic, no persuasion needed.** Cover the whole horizon, start the
14	   new price late, pick the cheap payment term, Incoterm, ppm and chargeback, keep the must-haves.
15	   Evidence: sandbox D01 went from 0.20 to 0.79 only because the LLM agent asked for 24 months
16	   instead of 12 and a later start. On P01 the start date is worth more than two euros of price.
17	2. **Price close to what the supplier would really accept.** That needs a target per case (its
18	   cost, its margin, how far it moved in the past) and enough rounds used well. On D01 the agent
19	   accepted after 4 of 10 rounds and left 8,580 on the table.
20	3. **Not losing the supplier.** Tone, a real trade for every ask, arguments whose figures check
21	   out, and for strategic suppliers a price that leaves them a sustainable margin.
22	
23	Everything in 1 is code and transfers to any hidden case. Most teams will leave it to the LLM.
24	We do it in code first.

184	## 6. How we test
185	
186	1. **Offline first.** With `C_open` and `C_best` known, `total_cost` gives the score of any term
187	   sheet for free. Most of part 1 above is tested this way.

189	   negotiations can be played for free and by the thousand. Twins of the suppliers we have played,
190	   each calibrated so that the best package it would accept costs exactly the case's `C_best`, plus
191	   invented suppliers on generated cases against overfitting. A tournament runner plays strategy
192	   variants against all of them and reports mean, worst case and the held-out cases. The lab is
193	   only as good as its model of the suppliers: it is backtested against our real sessions, and a
194	   strategy that wins there is a hypothesis until the sandbox or one practice case confirms it.
195	   Good for structure (levers, accept timing, final offers, several sheets, RFQ) and robustness;
196	   weak for wording and tone.

198	   backfire? How many rounds until `final_offer`? Does an RFQ thread time out while we wait on
199	   another? What does a cost-breakdown request return? Which opening gets the largest first move?

204	## 7. Risks
205	
206	- **Time in the final.** A round takes about 30 s including the supplier's reply; a wave gives
207	  about 6.5 usable minutes. Ten rounds do not fit, and an RFQ with three suppliers handled one after
208	  another fits even less. The runner needs parallel threads and a round budget.
209	- **Overfitting.** Up to a third of the hidden cases combine supplier and case types practice never
210	  shows. No rule may mention a practice case or supplier by name; everything is driven by the case
211	  file, the dossier and the calculator.
212	- **Silent LLM failure.** Today a failed call plays the naive move. Our fallback must be the
213	  calculator's best move, and the runner must log every fallback.
214	- **A wrong figure costs trust.** Arguments come from the argument bank only; the LLM may not
215	  write a number or an ID that code did not give it.
216	- **One machine, one key.** Decide the final machine today (open question in `docs/STATUS.md`).

218	## 8. Data access, timing and overfitting (decided Sat 15:20)
219	
220	**No vector database, no embeddings.** The data is small and keyed by ID: all 208 letters, e-mails
221	and notes together are 46 KB; everything written about one supplier is at most about 500 tokens;
222	reading it by `supplier_id` takes 0.1 ms. Similarity search would add a dependency, latency and
223	wrong hits and solve a problem we do not have. Instead:
224	
225	- **Dossier cache**: one command builds a file per supplier from SQL plus the full text of its
226	  documents; no LLM summary (the texts are short enough to pass whole). Runtime is a dictionary
227	  lookup by the case's `suppliers` and `parts`. Sunday 08:00: `uv run arena data`, run the command
228	  again, commit. Schema: section 10.
229	- **Optimal values are computed, never retrieved.** The best term sheet depends on the case's
230	  rates, options and must-haves, which are new in every hidden case. The calculator derives it from
231	  the case file in milliseconds. Storing "what worked on P01" and looking it up is overfitting.
232	- **A supplier with no dossier must still work**: hidden cases carry `facts` that exist only in
233	  the case file. The agent builds a minimal dossier from those at the start of the case.
234	
235	**Where the time goes.** The 60-second clock starts when the session opens and runs per thread.
236	Case files are readable before that (`GET /v1/cases?set=final` once the wave has started), so all
237	preparation happens **before** `POST /v1/sessions`: dossier lookup, plan, argument bank, and one
238	planning call to the LLM if we want one. Inside the session a move is the calculator (milliseconds)
239	plus one LLM call for the wording. Budget: 15 s per move as the target, 40 s as the hard deadline
240	after which the calculator's move is sent without the LLM. Nothing in a move may search or summarise.
241	
242	**Guards against overfitting** (the hidden set includes combinations practice never hosts):
243	
244	- No practice case ID, supplier ID or supplier name anywhere in code or prompts. Review for it.
245	- The calculator must handle **every** negotiable field. `incoterm` is negotiable in no practice
246	  case, `tooling_eur` in one, `effective_date` in two; the final may use any of them.
247	- Dry-run the whole pipeline (prepare, plan, first message) on all 19 practice case files, not only
248	  the 10 hosted ones. `P06` (rfq + stabilise) and `P13` (price_increase + leverage) are
249	  combinations that are never hosted, which is what the final will look like.
250	- Property tests on generated case files: random negotiable sets, options, must-haves and goals.
251	  Every proposed sheet has exactly the negotiable fields, values from `term_options`, keeps the
252	  must-haves and has a finite C.
253	- Hold out 3 of the 10 hosted cases (P04, P10, P18): never look at them while tuning, play them
254	  only in full runs. If the held-out mean falls behind the others, we are overfitting.
255	- Judge a change by the mean over cases, never by one case.

265	## 10. The dossier and the mini-dossier (schema decided Sat 17:41)
266	
267	One schema for both. The **dossier** is built offline for each of the 46 detailed suppliers. The
268	**case overlay** is added at session open from the case file and the opening e-mails; for a
269	supplier we have no data on it is the whole dossier (the mini-dossier). Fixed now so A and B build
270	against the same thing. A better data point found later costs little: add the field, run the
271	builder again.
272	
273	**Change rule.** Fields marked `*` are read by code (calculator, argument bank): their names and
274	meaning are frozen for `schema_version` 1. Any field may be added at any time. Renaming or removing
275	a `*` field needs a `schema_version` bump and a `[decision]` in the log.
276	
277	**Interface** (`sellm/intel.py`):
278	
279	- `uv run python -m sellm.intel build` writes `sellm/dossiers/<supplier number>.json` for every
280	  detailed supplier plus `index.json`. Deterministic (sorted keys, no LLM, no network), under 10 s,
281	  **committed**, so the final machine needs no rebuild. Rebuild and commit after the Sunday release.
282	- `dossier(supplier_id, part_ids, case=None, opening=None, package=None) -> dict`: the stored
283	  dossier restricted to `part_ids` (parts it does not supply are built live from the package), with
284	  the case overlay merged in. `opening` is the threads dict as in `decide(case, threads)` (a thread
285	  may be a list or `{"messages": [...]}`); `package` a DataPackage or its path, default
286	  `$ARENA_DATA`. Never raises; for an unknown supplier it returns the overlay alone
287	  (`coverage: "case_only"`). A blocked old vendor record whose company lives on under a detailed
288	  record of the same name is mapped to it (in the data: `sup:71999` -> `sup:70210`), with a warning.
289	  About 1 ms per call once the package is loaded (the first call loads it, about 0.1 s).
290	- `citable` is filled by `sellm.claims.citable_for(package, supplier_id, part_ids)` (group C); the
291	  builder and the overlay call it. `arguments(case, supplier_id, dossier)` (group C) turns it into
292	  sentences for the negotiator.
293	- Units as in the data: prices per the part's `price_unit`; yearly rates as fractions (0.09);
294	  percentages as numbers (9.5).
295

332	
333	**Rules for the derived fields.** Initial rules; calibrate them in the lab and change them only in
334	the builder.
335	
336	- `should_cost`: the row whose `supplier_id` is this supplier (`cost:310012-70110` for Brandlhuber,
337	  not `cost:310012`, which is Wimbacher's plant); else the generic row without a supplier. Another
338	  supplier's plant estimate is never this supplier's should-cost and is not cited to it.
339	- `floor_estimate`: plant-specific should-cost, value = unit_cost, band = its `confidence_pct`
340	  (floors came out within 3-5 % of it, `docs/LEARNINGS.md`); generic German should-cost times the
341	  country factor (AT, CH 1.05; CZ, PL, HU 0.825; TR 0.75; CN 0.7), band 15 %; none: null, and the
342	  calculator falls back to a share of the opening.
343	- `cost_of_money`: with skonto terms, `skonto_pct / 100 * 360 / (payment_days - skonto_days)` (2 %
344	  at 10 days instead of 30 is 0.36); else archetype `job_shop` or `cash_short` strength 2 or more:
345	  0.25 (P05's Czech job shop measured about 0.35); else group 0.065 (P02, P08), family 0.09 (D01),
346	  founder or private 0.10; plus 0.05 if the credit index is 300 or more or rose 20 points or more in
347	  12 months. The skonto rate is measured, so it gets no surcharge (calibrated Sat 18:30).
348	  The credit index is higher-is-worse (groups 147-178; the two cash-short skonto suppliers rose to 302
349	  and 343).
350	- `cash_pressure`: `high` with skonto terms or `cash_short` strength 2 or more; `medium` with an
351	  equity ratio under 25 %, a credit index of 250 or more, or a rising credit index; else `low`.
352	- `archetype`: `group` if the owner type is group; else `job_shop` if staff < 80 or cash pressure is
353	  high; else `family` if family-owned; else `trader` for raw material or a quote remark "supply from
354	  stock"; `monopolist` overrides when
355	  `capacity_tight` or `list_price_fixed` is signalled and the part has no alternative; else `other`.
356	- `citable`: only what the arena accepts (an `idx` pair is one series, at most 12 months apart,
357	  ending within the last 12 months of the data). Every entry is checked with `sellm/lab/claims.py`
358	  at build time: 0 `contradicted`. Facts that help the supplier (a rising index) stay in with
359	  `helps_buyer: false`, so A knows what the supplier may cite.
360	
361	**Signal kinds** (`signals[].kind`, frozen vocabulary: add kinds, do not rename). Strength is
362	min(3, distinct pieces of evidence): one per text, one per structured condition; a news item found by
363	its topic and by its words counts once. Noise news and market news never count. Rules and patterns:
364	`sellm/intel/signals.py` (calibrated Sat 18:30 against all 46 suppliers' texts).
365	
366	| Kind | Evidence in the data | What it means for us |
367	|---|---|---|
368	| `cash_short` | "Could you pay our invoices within 10 days?", liquidity, "the bank", skonto terms, quote remark "Payment within 10 days requested", news `credit_downgrade`, `credit_watch`, `short_time_work`. A low equity ratio is not evidence here; it raises `cash_pressure` to `medium` | trade faster payment for price; it values payment days at its high cost of money; do not squeeze its margin |
369	| `wants_volume` | "focus on customers with volume", idle shop floor, news `free_capacity`, "accepted below full cost to keep the volume" | a longer contract, full-need coverage or a bundle buys price |
370	| `capacity_tight` | news `allocation`, `full_order_book`, `big_order`, `chip_shortage` | secure volume and lead time first; price moves little |
371	| `list_price_fixed` | "head-office directive", "list conditions" in quote remarks; "no room on price this year: head office has frozen all price reductions" | do not fight the list price; move payment, start date, freight, chargeback |
372	| `material_hedged` | "material covered until ..." | index arguments are weak until then; ask for a later start or a fixed price |
373	| `partnership` | past favours and the reciprocity asked for ("kept supplying at the old price ... expects partnership in return"), "long-standing", "for generations". Read from the text, not the subject: "Visit by the owner" notes are often about something else, and the vendor-master date is 1996-01-01 for 36 of 46 suppliers | appreciation and reciprocity; never an ultimatum |
374	| `margin_floor` | "cannot sign anything that lowers our margin"; a part priced at or below its plant-specific should-cost (e.g. Wimbacher 310012 at 0.97) | the price is near its floor; trade terms, not price |
375	| `quality_problem` | latest scorecard amber or red, ppm above 1,500, an overdue 8D (each condition counts once), 8D/complaint/defect in its texts | lever for ppm commitment and chargeback; cite `sc` and `qn` |
376	| `delivery_problem` | latest on-time delivery below 75 % (9 of 46; below the 95 % target are 43 of 46, which says nothing); strength 2 below 65 %, 3 below 55 % | cite OTD; ask for a lead-time commitment |
377	| `ownership_change` | news `new_owner`, `succession`, `restructuring`, `refocus` | new decision makers, risk that it walks; be clear and fair |
378	| `approval_ladder` | owner type group or a group parent, "head office", "price changes above 2 % need the approval of their pricing committee" | expect a round on hold before a bigger move; be patient |
379	| `price_claim` | a letter with `asked_pct` and stated reasons; in the opening e-mail "<series> rose x % in twelve months and is y % of our cost" | check each stated cost driver against its index; cite the ones that fell |
380	| `informal_costing` (added Sat 18:30) | "works from his own spreadsheet, last updated two years ago", "had not followed his material and energy prices closely since the 2022 peak; his office manager does the costing" | the supplier does not track its own costs: one verified index figure can disarm it ("we didn't know that"); bring exactly one strong figure |
381	
382	**The case overlay** (mini-dossier): at session open, before the first move, under 100 ms, no LLM.
383	
384	- `identity` from the vendor master if the ID is known (also the about 400 suppliers known only by
385	  name, category and spend), else the name from the opening e-mail.
386	- `standard_terms` from the quote PDF (`arena_kit.docs.standard_terms`), overriding stored values.
387	- `signals` from the briefing, the trigger doc, the quote e-mail and PDF remarks, and any `doc:` or
388	  `news:` in the case's `facts`.
389	- `citable` from the case's `facts` (a dict keyed by ID like `facts.json`, as the Calculator already
390	  reads it; accept a list too) and its `refs`.
391	- `should_cost` and `floor_estimate` from a `cost:` fact of the case.
392	- `alternatives` from `buyer.alternative` and, in an RFQ, the other suppliers' offers (their
393	  `offer:` IDs are citable in the session).
394	- Merge: lists are united by ID; scalar values from the case win.
395	- `alternatives` entries from the case carry a `kind`: `buyer_alternative` (our alternative quote,
396	  marked on the existing entry if the quote is already listed), `current_contract`, `rfq_rival`
397	  (another bidder's opening offer with its `offer_id`). All are buyer-private.
398

401	without raising (B's tests). 0 `contradicted` in `citable` and in every sentence `arguments()`

1	# Sandbox probes: how the suppliers react (Sat 2026-10-10, 15:42-15:57)
2	
3	33 sandbox sessions, no practice quota used. Script: `experiments/sandbox_probes.py`. Raw summaries:
4	`experiments/results/`. Every session in full: `runs/sandbox/D01/` and `runs/sandbox/D02/`, labelled
5	`probe <name>` in `runs/README.md`.
6	
7	**All of this was measured on the three demo suppliers of the sandbox** (a family foundry in D01, a
8	German job shop and a Polish machining company in D02). Samples are 2-3 sessions per variant.
9	Treat the mechanics (sections 1, 2, 4) as how the arena works, and the price dynamics (section 3)
10	as a strong hypothesis to confirm on practice suppliers of other types.
11	
12	## 1. Only the first term sheet of an e-mail can be accepted (H1: refuted, with a way round)
13	
14	- Accepting an alternative by its ID (`offer:...-a`) fails with `422 not a standing offer in this
15	  session`, in the round it was offered (h1a, 2 of 2) and one round later (h1b, 2 of 2). A 422 costs
16	  nothing, the session goes on.
17	- **Way round (h1c, 2 of 2):** send the alternative's exact terms back as our own term sheet. The
18	  supplier answers `agreed` with those terms as its standing sheet, and that one can be accepted.
19	  It costs one message and took 8 s.
20	
21	So when a supplier's second package is cheaper for us by C: one extra round, then accept.
22	
23	## 2. After `final_offer` (H2)
24	
25	All sessions reached `final_offer` on the scripted path; then one more message:
26	
27	| Our answer to `final_offer` | n | What happened |
28	|---|---|---|
29	| lower price only (`h2-push`) | 2 | once unchanged, **once the supplier walked away: no deal, score 0** |
30	| lower price plus a give, here an earlier start (`h2-trade`) | 2 | once unchanged; once repriced to the new date at 0.10 less, which cost us 50 more in C |
31	| same price, later start (`h2-shift`) | 2 | refused twice, offer unchanged |
32	| holding message, no term sheet, no ask (`h2-hold`) | 2 | offer unchanged, new offer ID, accepted without trouble |
33	
34	- **A final offer is final.** Nothing was gained after it in 6 attempts, and a plain price push
35	  lost the deal once in two.
36	- **A holding message keeps the offer alive** and restarts the 60-second clock. It costs a message
37	  and about 15 s.
38	- The gain has to be made **before** `final_offer` (section 3).
39	
40	## 3. The supplier mirrors our steps, not our level (H8, H10: new)
41	
42	D01, same terms in every session (30 days, 24 months, start February), only the opening ask and
43	the size of our concession per message varied:
44	
45	| Opening ask | Our step per message | n | Supplier's final price | Score | Messages until `final_offer` |
46	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
47	| 50.00 | 0.05 | 3 | 51.40, 51.40, 51.40 | 0.676 | 4 |
48	| 50.00 | 0.15 | 8 | 50.70-51.00, mean 50.86 | 0.75-0.80 | 6 |
49	| 49.00 | 0.15 | 3 | 51.00, 50.60, 51.00 | 0.75-0.82 | 6 |
50	| 48.60 | 0.30 | 3 | 50.80, 50.40, 50.70 | 0.79-0.86 | 6 |
51	| 48.00 | 0.40 | 3 | 50.20, 50.30, 50.20 | **0.88-0.90** | 6 |
52	
53	- The supplier's first counter was 51.50 in all 20 sessions, whatever we opened with (48.00 to 50.00).
54	- After that it gave back roughly 0.6 to 0.85 of each step we made. Tiny steps got tiny steps and an
55	  early `final_offer`.
56	- **Opening lower alone changed nothing** (49.00 against 50.00 at the same step: same result).
57	  **Moving more did**: every increase of our step lowered the final price.
58	- `final_offer` came at our 6th message in every session with steps of 0.15 or more.
59	
60	What follows: plan about five concessions, open low enough that five sizeable steps still end
61	below the supplier's price, and make every message a visible move. The kit's LLM agent does the
62	opposite: it starts close and shrinks its steps (P07: 5.00, 5.10, 5.20, 5.25).
63	
64	Not known yet: where this stops (the supplier's cost floor; C_best in D01 corresponds to about
65	49.65 on these terms, the best run reached 50.20), whether asks below the current price (48.60)
66	cost goodwill with a real supplier, and how a group with an approval ladder or a near-monopolist reacts.
67	
68	## 4. RFQ: the 60-second clock (H3)
69	
70	| Variant | n | Timeouts per session | Deal | Score |
71	|---|---|---|---|---|
72	| kit `play()`, one thread at a time (`h3-seq`) | 2 | 2 (one on each thread) | job shop, `agreed` at 15.30 and 15.00 | 0.492, 0.441 |
73	| rounds in lockstep, a ready thread held back (first try of `h3-par`) | 1 | 2 | **the cheaper supplier withdrew**; closed with the other at 16.10 | 0.239 |
74	| one loop per thread, accept the first ready thread if cheapest (`h3-par`) | 2 | **0** | job shop, `final_offer` at 15.40 | 0.345, 0.345 |
75	| scripted, citing the rival's offer by ID (`h11`) | 2 | 0 | job shop, `agreed` at 15.50 DAP | 0.461, 0.461 |
76	
77	- **One loop per thread removes the timeouts.** Each thread answers as soon as its own reply
78	  arrives; replies took 30 to 59 s, so waiting for the slowest thread breaks the others' clocks.
79	- **Never leave a thread at `final_offer` waiting.** The job shop, at `final_offer`, was left for
80	  over a minute while the other thread went on. When we came back to accept, it had withdrawn: "We
81	  need to plan our machine time, so I am closing this RFQ." Accept at once, or send a holding message.
82	- **How a timeout works:** it is counted when the session is next touched, once, however long the
83	  silence was. The supplier then sends a follow-up with a **new offer ID** (the old one is no
84	  longer acceptable) and may harden: the Polish supplier went from `open` to `final_offer` at the
85	  same price. `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` shows `seconds_left` per thread. Accepting the re-issued
86	  offer inside the new 60 s worked.
87	- **Removing the timeouts did not raise the score here.** The sequential runs happened to get the
88	  better price. What we ask decides the score; the clock decides whether a supplier is still there.
89	- **A rival's offer cited by its ID is `verified`**; citing the same ID again is `duplicate`. Offer
90	  IDs change every round, so there is always a fresh one.
91	- **An early `agreed` means we asked too little**: in `h11` the job shop agreed to our second ask
92	  at once. C_best in D02 is 156,739; the best we closed is about 186,000. Both suppliers have far more
93	  room than any run found.
94	
95	## 5. Rules for our agent
96	
97	1. Price every sheet in an e-mail by C. To take a second sheet, send its terms back, wait for
98	   `agreed`, accept.
99	2. Never push the price after `final_offer`. Accept, or hold once if another thread needs a minute.
100	3. Open low and concede in about five large, visible steps; keep every ask below the supplier's
101	   standing price. Never repeat an ask and never shrink the steps early.
102	4. In an RFQ run one loop per thread. No thread may wait on another.
103	5. Accept a thread at `final_offer` within its 60 seconds, or hold it. After any timeout re-read the
104	   thread: the offer ID has changed.
105	6. If the supplier says `agreed` early, the ask was too high: the next case of that kind needs a
106	   lower opening.
107

133	### 7.1 The supplier prices in value, not in price

24	| P01 | price_increase / stabilise | 0.789 | 5 | open (held its price twice) | 133.70, 14 d, from Jan 2027 | 11,995 | start date (April is worth 14,556) |
25	| P04 | renewal / routine | 0.810 | 3 | final_offer | 4.91, 60 d, 24 m | 441 | payment term (90 d is worth 1,309) |
26	| P03 | renewal / stabilise | 0.903 | 4 | open | 432.94, 90 d, 36 m, 4,580/y | 32,587 | price |
27	
28	Score points lost, of 10 possible: 3.85. Three cases (P02, P18, P08) account for 2.09 of them.
29	
30	## What the baseline shows
31	
32	Each finding says how sure it is: **seen** in these sessions, **computed** offline with the cost
33	function, or **open** (a hypothesis).
34	
35	### 1. The agent stops as soon as the supplier stops moving (seen, all cases)
36	
37	It accepted on the first `final_offer` (7 cases), on `agreed` (P11) or when the supplier repeated
38	its price (P01, P03). It used 2 to 5 of its 10 messages; in P10 it accepted after two. It never
39	tests whether a final offer is final, and never brings a new trade once the supplier says "final". What a supplier does
40	when we answer a final offer with a different package instead of a lower price is **open**: test
41	it in the sandbox before building on it.
42	
43	### 2. It looks only at the supplier's first term sheet (seen; cost computed)
44	
45	Suppliers often send two packages in one e-mail; alternatives appeared in 11 of 12 threads. The
46	kit's `standing()` reads `term_sheets[0]` and never prices the second.
47	
48	- **P10**: Ravensteiner offered 33.80 with 42 days lead time, and as the alternative
49	  (`offer:70410-1-a`) 32.00 with 54 days. The alternative costs C 1,541,719 (score 0.647). The
50	  agent insisted on 42 days and closed at 33.60, C 1,588,298 (score 0.570). It paid 1.60 more per
51	  seal on 46,800 seals (the two years that count), about 74,900, to save 12 days of lead time
52	  that cost us 2,400 a day, about 28,800.
53	- **P02**: 372.30 at 60 days was on the table and is cheaper for us than the accepted 370.15 at 30 days.
54	
55	Rule for our agent: price **every** sheet a supplier sends and compare by C, not by unit price.
56	Whether an alternative can be accepted by its ID (`...-a`) in the same or a later round is **open**.
57	
58	### 3. An RFQ handled thread by thread times out (seen, P05)
59	
60	`play()` sends one message and waits for the reply while the other threads' 60-second clocks run.
61	P05 recorded two timeouts on sup:70210, two on sup:70250, and sup:70240 - the cheapest opening at
62	31.50 - withdrew after a late message. The timeout replies read "Without movement from your side
63	we cannot move either." We closed with the supplier that had opened highest (38.50 -> 29.50).
64	C_best corresponds to about 26.71. The runner must write to all threads of a case in parallel.
65	
66	### 4. Data arguments are barely used, and repeated (seen)
67	
68	Across 12 threads: 8 claims `verified`, 8 `duplicate`, 0 `contradicted`. Three cases had none at
69	all (P05, P07, P08). The duplicates are the same ID cited again in a later e-mail, which earns
70	nothing. Suppliers asked for data outright - "Which figures is that based on? Please send us the
71	data." in P03, P05 and P10, "Please provide the data supporting your assumptions" in P04 - and the
72	agent had nothing to send, because it only sees what the case's `refs` point to.
73	
74	### 5. Should-cost is the missing price anchor (computed)
75	
76	Price at C_best with the best non-price terms (relationship term not included, so slightly low for
77	`stabilise` and `secure_supply`), against the should-cost estimate where one exists for the
78	supplier's own plant:
79	
80	| Case | Should-cost | Current price | Opening | Our deal | Price at C_best | Deal / should-cost | C_best / should-cost |
81	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
82	| P01 | 132.64 | 126.53 | 138.55 | 133.70 | 138.2 (with April start and 90 d) | 1.01 | 1.04 |
83	| P02 | 374.95 | 348.32 | 370.96 | 370.15 | 368.1 | 0.99 | 0.98 |
84	| P03 | 403.21 | 412.74 | 438.21 | 432.94 | 429.4 | 1.07 | 1.07 |
85	| P10 | 24.31 | 29.89 | 32.20 | 33.60 | 28.1 | **1.38** | 1.16 |
86	| P05 | 36.87 (generic, German cost base) | 36.39 | 31.50-38.50 | 29.50 | 26.7 | 0.80 | 0.72 |
87	
88	For the four cases with a plant-specific estimate, C_best sits between 0.98 and 1.16 times
89	should-cost. That gives a target before the first e-mail. In P10 we paid 38 % above the supplier's
90	estimated full cost and never cited `cost:340010`. P05's suppliers include a Czech shop, which the
91	company's rule of thumb puts at 0.8-0.85 of the German cost base. Cases without a should-cost row
92	(P04, P07, P08, P11, P18) need another anchor: **open**.
93	
94	### 6. Non-price terms: what was left, and one trade that worked (computed)
95	
96	- **P01**: an April start was never asked for. At the deal's price and 14-day payment it is worth
97	  14,556, more than the whole gap of 11,995. The supplier said "the 14-day payment term is essential
98	  for us to offer our best price": it wants cash. Keep 14 days, ask for April.
99	- **P02**: 90 instead of 30 days is worth 30,155 of the 42,371 gap. Nordmark prices longer terms
100	  ("the premium for extended payment terms is reflected in the price difference between the
101	  packages"), so the question is whether its premium is smaller than our gain. From its two
102	  packages: 2.15 per unit for 30 more days, about 13,100, against 15,100 for us.
103	- **P08, P18**: the case expects the alloy index to rise 6 %, so an index clause costs us. No clause
104	  is worth 9,453 (P08) and 2,389 (P18); 90-day payment 7,003 and 1,770. Werdenfels refused a fixed
105	  price for 24 months ("indexation is necessary to manage material volatility").
106	- **P11, a trade that worked**: the agent gave up the chargeback (500 -> 0 per complaint, worth
107	  2,146 to us) and got 1.00 off the price (worth 15,900). Give what is cheap for us and valuable to them.
108	- **Coverage was right everywhere**: no case lost points on uncovered need. The LLM handles this;
109	  the naive agent did not (D01).
110	
111	### 7. Where C_best is far below anything we argued for (open)
112	
113	P18: C_best is at about 4.73, 19 % below the *current* price of 5.84. P08: 5.10 against 5.45.
114	P10: 28.1 against 29.89. In these cases the supplier would accept far less than it shows, and we
115	do not know yet which fact unlocks it. Candidates to check in the data before spending sessions:
116	the split between base price and alloy surcharge (the P08/P18 titles name it), Donautal's remark
117	that its material "is covered at fixed prices until March", the second-source quotes, the notes
118	and letters of these three suppliers. The alloy index itself rose 5.9 % in twelve months
119	(2,839.7 in 2025-09 to 3,007.8 in 2026-09) but fell 5.5 % since June.
120	
121	### 8. The relationship term is small so far (seen)
122	
123	Charged by the arena: P01 813, P03 337, P02 0, P10 0. None of the baseline deals squeezed a
124	strategic supplier. There is room on price before that term matters.
125	
126	### 9. Time is fine for single-supplier cases (seen)
127	
128	Ten cases in parallel finished in four minutes. A round takes about 30 s including the supplier's
129	reply. Using all ten rounds would take about five to six minutes per case, close to the limit of a
130	final wave (6.5 usable minutes).
131	
132	## Hypotheses to test, cheapest first
133	
134	| # | Hypothesis | How | Cost |
135	|---|---|---|---|
136	| H1 | A supplier's alternative sheet can be accepted by its ID | sandbox D01 or D02 | free |
137	| H2 | Answering `final_offer` with a different package (not a lower price) gets another move instead of a walk-away | sandbox | free |
138	| H3 | Writing to all RFQ threads in parallel removes the timeouts and keeps the cheapest bidder in | sandbox D02, then P05 | free, then 1 |
139	| H4 | P01: keeping 14-day payment and asking for an April start reaches about 1.0 | P01 | 1 |
140	| H5 | P10: taking the 54-day package and citing `cost:340010` (24.31) beats 0.647 | P10 | 1 |
141	| H6 | P02: asking for 90 days and pricing every package by C lifts the score above 0.5 | P02 | 1 |
142	| H7 | P08/P18: there is a fact in the data that justifies a base price well below today's | data first, then 1 each | 0, then 2 |
143	
144	Record each result in `docs/LEARNINGS.md` and log it as a `[run]`.
145	
146	**Update Sat 15:57:** H1, H2 and H3 are tested in the sandbox, with two follow-ups. H1 is refuted
147	(only the first sheet can be accepted; send the alternative's terms back instead), a final offer
148	is final, per-thread loops remove the RFQ timeouts, and the supplier mirrors the size of our
149	concessions. Details: `experiments/RESULTS.md`.

2	
3	Omar's questions: is the first ask (target x 0.94) too high and should it be dynamic; how far can the
4	target be pushed before a supplier quits; is the 4-round horizon too short; can relationship
5	suppliers be pushed harder; what would knowing the supplier's should-cost gain. Full report (German,
6	for Omar and the team): https://claude.ai/code/artifact/cd7f860c-5e80-433d-b1fe-40bb34782ddf
7	
8	**Result: none of the price levers gains on average; today's open_below 0.06, horizon 4 and target
9	sit at the optimum. In the lab a better cost estimate for unknown suppliers looked worth up to +2
10	points, but the arena check (section "Arena check") gave -2.4: no lever is left in the price path.
11	Never ask after a final offer.**
12	
13	## Sources
14	
15	- Real sessions in `runs/` (all agents, practice and sandbox): 316 threads from 200 sessions with a
16	  calibrated floor (`sellm/lab/twins.json` personas' `full_cost`, set so the cheapest acceptable package
17	  costs the real `C_best`; P05's RFQ floors are synthetic and left out of the per-case figures).

19	  scenarios (12 fitted twins, 200 invented) x 3 seeds = 18,444 negotiations, engine suppliers, clock on,

21	  `runs/lab/20261011-0031-price-path-up/summary.json`. Differences are paired (same scenario and seed)
22	  against `sellm.agent.make_agent` at 20a318a, in points on the 100 scale, +- standard error.

26	| Question | Real sessions | Lab (paired, all scenarios) |
27	|---|---|---|

30	| Walk-aways | 6 in 316 threads: 4 after a push past final_offer (practice 3 of 4 such pushes withdrew), 2 in P05 with a first ask 13.6 % below the floor | push_final 0.005 -0.49, 0.01 -4.77 (twins -21.06, 59 more lost deals) |
31	| Horizon | final_offer after a median of 4 of our messages, in 64 % after at most 4 (171 threads) | 3 -0.27, **4**, 6 -0.26, 8 -0.83, 10 -1.26 (twins 6 -1.40, 8 -3.99, 10 -6.58) |
32	| Relationship push | stabilise/secure_supply suppliers end closer to the floor (1.060 vs 1.096) but give a smaller share of their room (0.32 vs 0.40); walk-aways 2 % in both | only in relationship cases: horizon 6 -0.03, open 0.10 -1.11, target x0.95 -1.09; per twin D01 +4.7..+5.2, P01 +5.6..+6.3, P02 -2.8..-3.4; invented relationship suppliers lose for every archetype |
33	| Should-cost known (oracle) | today: own-plant should-cost +1.4..+2.1 % (P10 -5.2 %), priors -2.2..+10.8 % | exact floor, first ask 6 % below -1.74; 3 % below +1.71; at the floor +1.97; floor +5 % **+2.05**; floor -5 % **-5.89**; twins all -0.4..-2.9, invented +1.8..+2.3 |
34	
35	## Arena check (Sun 00:40-01:05, 8 practice sessions, 4 free D01 sessions)
36	
37	One session per case (practice suppliers answer identical messages identically); baseline = the
38	22:25 full run, which today's agent replays move for move. `experiments/price_path_arena.py`, rows in
39	`experiments/results/2026-10-11-price-path.json`, sessions labelled `PRICE-PATH ...`.
40	
41	| Variant | Case | Today | Arena | Difference | Lab predicted |
42	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
43	| horizon 6 | P07 | 0.747 | 0.702 | -0.045 | -0.035 |
44	| horizon 6 | P11 | 0.778 | 0.710 | -0.068 | -0.059 |
45	| horizon 6 | P18 | 0.467 | 0.401 | -0.066 | -0.050 |
46	| horizon 6 | D01 | 0.947 | 0.921 | -0.026 | -0.013 |
47	| oracle, first ask 3 % below the floor | P02 | 0.531 | 0.531 | 0 | +0.019 |
48	| oracle, first ask 3 % below the floor | P07 | 0.747 | 0.766 | +0.019 | -0.009 |
49	| oracle, first ask 3 % below the floor | P11 | 0.778 | 0.710 | -0.068 | -0.011 |
50	| oracle, first ask 3 % below the floor | P18 | 0.467 | 0.406 | -0.061 | +0.039 |
51	| oracle, first ask 3 % below the floor | D01 | 0.947 | 0.935 | -0.012 | -0.013 |
52	| relationship target x0.95 | P02 | 0.531 | 0.531 | 0 | -0.028 |
53	| relationship target x0.95 | D01 | 0.947 | 0.959 | +0.012 | +0.052 |

55	- Horizon 6 loses in 4 of 4 (mean -5.1 points): the lab had direction and size right.
56	- The oracle loses on average (-2.4): the lab overestimated it. P18 closed at 5.40 instead of 5.50,
57	  but the supplier moved the package to 30 days and an index clause without deadband, which costs more
58	  in total: a lower first ask pushed it back to its own terms.
59	- Relationship push: P02 the same deal, D01 +0.012 (D01 varies 0.921-0.947 with one agent).
60	- P11's 0.778 is one lucky path (experiments/PERSISTENCE.md P3); both -0.068 there may partly be that.

62	## What follows (for code changes)
63	
64	1. Keep `open_below` 0.06, `horizon` 4 and the target; write the measured curves next to the knobs.
65	2. Never ask after `final_offer` (`push_final` stays off); a test that the agent accepts a final offer.
66	3. Keep `past_target`; do not widen it into a general relationship push.

68	   should-cost. The lab's +2 points did not survive the arena (oracle -2.4 over five cases).
69	5. Look for points outside the price path: which checked fact moves which supplier (measure per

78	sessions are observational. Lab scores of single twins differ from the arena (P01: lab 0.726, real

3	Jonathan asked for a full practice run with the LLM, tool calling, and a decision with a confidence
4	on whether to take the supplier's offer, tested on five random cases. 15 practice sessions.
5	Code: `sellm/advisor.py` (`SELLM_LLM=shadow|apply`, off by default), `sellm/llm.py:chat_tools`, the

10	
11	1. It writes the e-mail around the move code has fixed (guards: required sentences word for word,
12	   no new figure, no leak; else the template).
13	2. It gives a verdict on the supplier's standing offer, A = take it now, B = keep negotiating. It
14	   can call three functions first: the calculator's cost of any price, the dossier's profile of
15	   the supplier, the checked facts we have left. The confidence is the probability the model puts on
16	   its letter, read from the token probabilities - computed, not asked.
17	
18	## Results
19	
20	Full run, LLM writes every e-mail, verdict logged only (`shadow`); reference = the same agent with
21	template e-mails (v1.4 run of 21:58; P01 from the test with both new rules):

63	  sessions a supplier withdrew in 10 threads - 6 after timeouts, 3 after we asked again past its

1	# ruff: noqa: E501  (long sentences and messages)
2	"""The negotiator behind `--agent sellm`.
3	
4	Every decision is a pure function of the case file and the threads: what we asked before is read
5	from our own e-mails in the thread, nothing is counted in the object. So a second call for the same
6	state returns the same move, a fresh agent picks a case up after a crash, and `agent.fallback` is
7	the agent itself (its numbers need no LLM).
8	
9	The price path follows what real suppliers did in the sandbox (docs/LOG.md Sat 18:22 and 20:30,
10	experiments/RESULTS.md section 3):
11	- a supplier gives back a share of each step we make (the foundry in D01 about half, the job shop
12	  in D02 all of it, and it asks for "bigger steps" when ours are small against the gap), for four
13	  to six of our messages, then says `final_offer`; nothing is gained after that;
14	- an opening about 10 % or more below its floor costs half of those rounds; 5-7 % below does not;
15	- so: open a few percent below our estimate of where it can end, then size every step from what
16	  the thread shows - the gap to its price, the rounds left and the share of our steps it has given
17	  back so far - so that the two prices meet at the last round. No step size is fixed in advance.
18	  We never ask at or above its price, and we accept its final offer.
19	
20	The terms around the price come from the cost calculator (`sellm/calculator.py`): our first ask is
21	the package that costs us least at the price we expect to end at - C prices uncovered need at the
22	fallback, so it decides how long and how much to commit, and it wants payment as late as possible.
23	Payment days are cash to the supplier too: we ask for the latest ones only from a supplier the
24	dossier calls relaxed about cash, keep the quoted ones for one short of cash, and send both as two
25	offers that cost us the same when we know nothing about it (a supplier answers the offer worth most
26	to it). Real suppliers answer on the structure we send and put their price on it (294 of 304
27	replies in runs/); from then on we ask on whichever structure it has quoted that is cheapest for
28	us in C. The price path runs in price; C decides between structures and between offers.
29	"""

49	    open_below=0.06,  # we open this share below our estimate of where it can end
50	    horizon=4,  # our messages until the prices should meet: suppliers said `final_offer` after 1 to 6 of them (median 4)
51	    pace=0.5,  # the share of our steps a supplier gives back, until the thread has shown its own
52	    keep_below=0.006,  # never ask closer than this share to its standing offer: it should make the last move
53	    floor_share=None,  # our target as a share of its opening when no should-cost exists; None: TARGET_SHARE
54	    rate_guess=0.08,  # its cost of money when the dossier does not say (ours: no bias on payment days)
55	    claims="bank",  # none | bank (one new checked figure per e-mail)
56	    max_holds=2,  # holding e-mails per RFQ thread whose offer waits while the others still move; then we close
57	    levers="ours",  # first ask: ours (the calculator's cheapest package) | theirs (its terms, need covered)
58	    dossier=True,  # read its cost of money and cash position from sellm.intel when a dossier exists

96	def structures(case):
97	    """Every combination of the negotiable non-price fields over the case's options."""
98	    fields = [f for f in case["negotiable"] if f != "unit_price"]
99	    options = [case.get("term_options", {}).get(f) or [None] for f in fields]
100	    for combo in itertools.product(*options):
101	        yield {f: v for f, v in zip(fields, combo, strict=True) if v is not None or f == "index_clause"}

104	def _distance(a, b):
105	    if a == b:
106	        return 0.0
107	    if isinstance(a, bool) or isinstance(b, bool) or a is None or b is None:
108	        return 1.0
109	    if isinstance(a, int | float) and isinstance(b, int | float):
110	        return min(1.0, abs(a - b) / max(abs(b), 1.0))
111	    try:
112	        return min(1.0, abs((date.fromisoformat(a) - date.fromisoformat(b)).days) / 365)
113	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
114	        return 1.0

118	    return tuple(sorted((f, repr(x)) for f, x in structure.items()))

121	class Thread:
122	    """One supplier's thread, read once: what it offers, what we asked, what closes on its standard terms."""
123	
124	    def __init__(self, case, sid, events):
125	        self.case, self.sid, self.events = case, sid, events
126	        self.theirs = [m for m in events if m.get("from") != "buyer"]
127	        self.ours = [m for m in events if m.get("from") == "buyer"]
128	        self.opening = next((m for m in self.theirs if m.get("term_sheets")), None)
129	        self.last = self.theirs[-1] if self.theirs else {}
130	        self.status = self.last.get("status")
131	        self.sheets = [s for s in self.last.get("term_sheets") or [] if s.get("terms")]
132	        self.asks = [m["term_sheets"][0]["terms"] for m in self.ours if m.get("term_sheets")]
133	        self.holds = sum(1 for m in self.ours if not m.get("term_sheets") and not m.get("action"))
134	        self.left = moves_left(case, events)
135	        std0 = {}
136	        for att in (self.opening or {}).get("attachments") or []:
137	            if att.get("name", "").startswith("quote") and att.get("text"):
138	                std0 = quote_terms(att["text"]).get("standard", {})
139	                break
140	        self.std0 = std0  # as quoted at the opening: the yardstick C_open is priced with these
141	        self.std = {**std0, **standard_terms(events)}  # later PDFs leave out what the offer now states
142	
143	    @property
144	    def fresh(self):
145	        """Its last e-mail answers a holding e-mail of ours: the offer ID we see is the current one."""
146	        if len(self.events) < 2:
147	            return False
148	        ours = self.events[-2]
149	        return ours.get("from") == "buyer" and not ours.get("term_sheets") and not ours.get("action")
150	
151	    @property
152	    def standing(self):
153	        """(term_sheet_id, terms) of its standing offer: only the first sheet can be accepted."""
154	        return (self.sheets[0].get("term_sheet_id"), self.sheets[0]["terms"]) if self.sheets else (None, {})
155	
156	    def filled(self, terms):
157	        """Its sheet with every negotiable field: what it leaves out closes on its standard terms."""
158	        return complete_offer(self.case, {**self.std, **{k: v for k, v in terms.items() if v is not None}})
159	
160	    def c(self, terms, estimate=None):
161	        if not terms or terms.get("unit_price") is None:
162	            return math.inf
163	        return total_cost(self.case, terms, self.std, estimate)
164	
165	    def valid(self, terms):
166	        return bool(terms) and terms.get("unit_price") is not None and must_haves_ok(self.case, terms, self.std)
167	
168	    def coverage(self, terms):
169	        """Share of the need over the horizon that a deal on these terms covers."""
170	        b, t = self.case["buyer"], closing_terms(self.case, terms, self.std)
171	        years = min(t["contract_months"] / 12 if t["contract_months"] else 1.0, b["horizon_years"])
172	        return min(t["volume_per_year"], b["need_per_year"]) * years / (b["need_per_year"] * b["horizon_years"])

175	class Negotiator:
176	    def __init__(self, package=None, writer=None, chat=None, dossier=None, **knobs):
177	        self.k = {**DEFAULTS, **knobs}
178	        if writer:
179	            self.k["writer"] = writer
180	        if isinstance(dossier, bool):  # make_agent(package, dossier=False): the knob, not an object
181	            self.k["dossier"] = dossier
182	        self.package, self.chat, self.dossier = package, chat, dossier
183	        self.fallback = self  # the numbers need no LLM, so the fallback is this agent
184	        self.stats = {"moves": 0, "errors": 0, "fallbacks": 0}
185	        self.name = "sellm " + " ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in knobs.items())
186	        self._memo = {}

188	    # -- the kit's interface ---------------------------------------------------------------------
189	    def decide(self, case, threads, focus=None):
190	        """`focus` (one loop per thread) asks for a move in that thread."""
191	        try:
192	            draft = self.move(case, threads, focus)
193	            decision = self.message(case, threads, draft)
194	            self.stats["moves"] += 1
195	            return decision
196	        except Exception:
197	            if os.environ.get("SELLM_STRICT") == "1":
198	                raise
199	            self.stats["errors"] += 1
200	            log.exception("%s: the negotiator failed, sending a safe move", case.get("case_id"))
201	            return self.rescue(case, threads, focus)

203	    def rescue(self, case, threads, focus):
204	        """When our own code fails: a holding e-mail (valid, restarts the clock, the offer stands),
205	        or, with no message left, the kit's closing move. Never an exception to the runner."""
206	        from arena_kit.play import closing_move, live_threads
207	
208	        live = live_threads(threads)
209	        sid = focus if focus in live else (live[0] if live else next(iter(threads)))
210	        if live and moves_left(case, threads[sid]) > 1:
211	            body = "Dear Sir or Madam,\n\nthank you for your offer. We are reviewing it internally and will revert shortly."
212	            return {
213	                "supplier_id": sid,
214	                "message": {"subject": f"Re: {case['title']}"[:300], "body": body, "term_sheets": []},
215	            }
216	        if live:
217	            return closing_move(case, threads)
218	        return {"supplier_id": sid, "message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}

220	    # -- the decision ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
221	    def move(self, case, threads, focus=None):
222	        """What to do next, as a draft: kind (ask, take_alternative, hold, accept, walk_away), the
223	        thread, the term sheets and the argument sentences."""
224	        views = {sid: Thread(case, sid, events) for sid, events in threads.items()}
225	        live = [v for v in views.values() if v.theirs and v.status not in ENDED]
226	        if not live:
227	            return {"kind": "walk_away", "sid": next(iter(threads))}
228	        key = (case.get("case_id"), "openings")
229	        if key not in self._memo:  # every bidder's opening e-mail, which the dossier's case overlay reads (rivals too)
230	            self._memo[key] = {w.sid: [w.opening] for w in views.values() if w.opening}
231	        key = (case.get("case_id"), "cheapest")
232	        if key not in self._memo:  # openings never change: the market level an RFQ bidder has to beat
233	            opened = [v.opening["term_sheets"][0]["terms"].get("unit_price") for v in views.values() if v.opening]
234	            self._memo[key] = min((p for p in opened if p), default=None)
235	        cost = {v.sid: self.offer_cost(case, v) for v in live}
236	        leader = min(live, key=lambda v: cost[v.sid]).sid
237	        # what a bidder has to beat: the cheapest standing offer of the others (plain C, as the arena scores it)
238	        plain = {v.sid: v.c(v.filled(v.standing[1])) if cost[v.sid] < math.inf else math.inf for v in live}
239	        rival = {v.sid: min((plain[w.sid] for w in live if w.sid != v.sid), default=math.inf) for v in live}
240	        movable = sorted(
241	            (v for v in live if not self.ready(case, v, rival[v.sid])), key=lambda v: (len(v.ours), cost[v.sid])
242	        )
243	        if focus is not None and focus in views and views[focus] in live:
244	            v = views[focus]
245	            if v in movable:
246	                return self.ask(case, v, views, live, rival[v.sid])
247	            if movable:  # its offer waits while other threads still move: it must not time out meanwhile
248	                if cost[v.sid] < math.inf and v.holds < self.k["max_holds"] and v.left > 1:
249	                    return {"kind": "hold", "sid": v.sid, "sheets": [], "n": len(v.asks)}
250	                if views[leader] not in movable:  # the others have had their extra rounds: take the best offer
251	                    return self.close(case, views, live, cost)
252	        if movable:  # with `focus` on a waiting thread this is a move for another one: its own loop sends it
253	            return self.ask(case, movable[0], views, live, rival[movable[0].sid])
254	        draft = self.close(case, views, live, cost)
255	        if focus is None and len(views) > 1 and draft["kind"] == "accept":
256	            # A runner that serves one thread at a time (the kit's `play()`) lets the others time out,
257	            # and a timeout replaces the offer ID: accepting the old one is refused (422) and stops the
258	            # kit's runner. A holding e-mail first brings this thread's state up to date - it is
259	            # answered at once, or refused as late with the new offer - and then the accept is valid.
260	            v = views[draft["sid"]]
261	            if not v.fresh and v.left > 1:
262	                return {"kind": "hold", "sid": v.sid, "sheets": [], "n": len(v.asks)}
263	        return draft

265	    def offer_cost(self, case, v):
266	        """C of its standing offer, the relationship term priced with our estimate; inf if it cannot be taken."""
267	        sheet_id, terms = v.standing
268	        if not sheet_id or not v.valid(terms):
269	            return math.inf
270	        return v.c(terms, self.estimate(case, v))

272	    def done(self, case, v, rival=math.inf):
273	        """We have nothing more to ask here: it said its last word, or our next step would meet its
274	        price or no longer beat the best other offer."""
275	        if v.status in READY:
276	            return True
277	        plan = self.plan(case, v, rival)
278	        return plan["capped"] or plan["enough"]
279	
280	    def ready(self, case, v, rival=math.inf):
281	        """Take or leave its standing offer: nothing more to ask, and none of its other sheets is better."""
282	        if v.left <= 0:
283	            return True
284	        if v.standing[1].get("unit_price") is None:
285	            return False  # it has not named a price yet
286	        return self.done(case, v, rival) and self.better_alternative(case, v) is None
287	
288	    def close(self, case, views, live, cost):
289	        """Accept the cheapest standing offer that keeps the must-haves - whether it is called final,
290	        agreed or still open - unless the alternative is the better deal. A deal no better than the
291	        opening scores 0, as walking away without an alternative does: then the deal is taken (a tie
292	        goes to more deals)."""
293	        alt = case["buyer"].get("alternative") or {}
294	        c_alt = total_cost(case, alt["terms"]) if (alt.get("terms") or {}).get("unit_price") else math.inf
295	        takable = [v for v in live if cost[v.sid] < math.inf]
296	        if not takable:
297	            return {"kind": "walk_away", "sid": live[0].sid}
298	        best = min(takable, key=lambda v: cost[v.sid])
299	        if c_alt < cost[best.sid]:
300	            return {"kind": "walk_away", "sid": live[0].sid}
301	        return {"kind": "accept", "sid": best.sid, "accept_id": best.standing[0]}
302	
303	    def ask(self, case, v, views, live, rival=math.inf):
304	        if v.standing[1].get("unit_price") is not None and self.done(case, v, rival):
305	            alt = self.better_alternative(case, v)
306	            if alt is not None:  # its own second package, sent back as ours: it answers `agreed`
307	                return {"kind": "take_alternative", "sid": v.sid, "sheets": [alt], "n": len(v.asks)}
308	        plan = self.plan(case, v, rival)
309	        body_before = [m.get("body") or "" for m in v.theirs[:-1]]
310	        prices = [self.offer_cost_plain(v, m) for m in v.theirs if m.get("term_sheets")]
311	        flags = {
312	            "they_moved": len(prices) > 1 and prices[-1] < prices[-2] - EPS,
313	            "asked_for_data": bool(ASKS_DATA.search(v.last.get("body") or "")),
314	            "repeat_data_request": any(ASKS_DATA.search(b) for b in body_before),
315	        }
316	        if self.k.get("opening_line"):  # experiments on wording only (experiments/ab_sandbox.py)
317	            flags["opening_line"] = self.k["opening_line"]
318	        if not v.asks and v.opening:
319	            theirs = v.filled(v.opening["term_sheets"][0]["terms"]).get("contract_months")
320	            ours = plan["sheet"].get("contract_months")
321	            if "contract_months" in case["negotiable"] and ours and theirs is not None and ours > theirs:
322	                flags["commitment"] = f"{ours} months"
323	        arguments = self.arguments(case, v, views, live, plan["sheet"]) if self.k["claims"] == "bank" else []
324	        return {
325	            "kind": "ask",
326	            "sid": v.sid,
327	            "sheets": [plan["sheet"], *(self.menu(case, v, plan["sheet"]) if not v.asks else [])],
328	            "arguments": arguments,
329	            "n": len(v.asks),
330	            "flags": flags,
331	        }

333	    @staticmethod
334	    def offer_cost_plain(v, message):
335	        return v.c(v.filled(message["term_sheets"][0]["terms"]))
